title: Synthetic cold-start + customer-promptset rerank eval instrumentation and A/B hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Several customers have reported regressions in reranking relevance after model swaps and quantization changes. Existing evals focus on large aggregated promptsets and offline NDCG/MRR bootstraps but lack: (1) reproducible cold-start scenarios for new customers, (2) direct mapping between customer promptset slices and live A/B traffic, and (3) lightweight hooks to surface incremental changes to Console.

Goal: Instrument a unified rerank evaluation pipeline that supports (a) synthetic cold-start promptset generation, (b) ingestion of customer-provided promptsets with deterministic sampling, (c) continuous NDCG and MRR tracking per-customer slice, and (d) low-overhead A/B testing hooks so production traffic can be routed to variant ranks and recorded for offline validation. The primary deliverable is an end-to-end runbook + implementation that produces per-customer NDCG/MRR trends in the Console and ties individual A/B experiments to evaluation artifacts.

Scope: - Batch and streaming eval instrumentation for the reranker endpoint (embeddings + scoring) - Synthetic promptset generator to simulate cold-start query distributions (supporting n-gram diversity, long-tail queries, and session-style sequences) - A/B tagging and lightweight telemetry capture (bound to existing tracing) - Per-slice evaluation dashboard and nightly backfills - API surface for customers to upload promptsets for private eval runs

Non-goals: Full large-scale trainer integration or automated rollback policies (those belong to rollout/ops). This ticket focuses on telemetry + eval instrumentation and hooks for linking to canaries.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Synthetic generator that emits >10k cold-start queries with configurable distribution parameters and unit tests to validate diversity metrics
2) Ingestion pipeline for customer promptsets with deterministic sharding and sampling documented in Confluence
3) NDCG@10 and MRR@10 computed daily for each customer slice and stored in metrics platform with tags: customer_id, promptset_id, run_id, model_variant
4) A/B hook that can mark live requests as experiment=control|variant and persist minimal telemetry (query_id, timestamp, variant, reranker_scores) with <5% added p50 latency overhead
5) Console dashboard showing per-customer NDCG/MRR timeseries and ability to link a timeseries point to the underlying evaluation run artifacts
6) End-to-end integration test that runs a small synthetic cold-start eval, triggers an A/B tagged request on staging, and verifies metrics propagation to Console
7) Documentation: runbook with steps for running private promptset evals and interpreting metrics
tasks: Design data model for eval runs and metric tags (engineers + metrics)
Implement synthetic promptset generator library and unit tests
Extend promptset ingestion API to accept customer uploads and compute deterministic shards
Add NDCG/MRR calculator module with efficient incremental update hooks
Instrument rerank endpoint to emit AB tags and minimal telemetry payloads
Create nightly backfill job for existing promptsets and one-off customer replays
Wire metrics to Console dashboard and add drilldown links to eval artifacts
Write Confluence runbook and example scripts for SEs to onboard customer promptsets
Create GitHub PRs and request code review from Ranking and Observability owners
notes_or_decisions: Decision 2025-02-18: Use NDCG@10 and MRR@10 as primary evals; store raw relevance judgments to allow other metrics later
Decision 2025-02-25: Telemetry payload will be minimised to avoid tokenization or sensitive data; store query hash and reference to promptset entry rather than raw text
Sampling: deterministic hashing on (customer_id, prompt_id) to ensure repeatable slices across runs
Storage: eval runs will be stored in S3 under evals/{customer_id}/{run_ts} and referenced by run_id in metrics
Design tradeoff: Accept small p50 latency increase on staging (target <5% relative) for AB telemetry; production rollout will gate this behind canary flag
